cards.text: Jesus just healed a man's withered hand on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees walked out plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Him (Mark 3:5-6). So Jesus withdraws with His disciples to the sea. The SEA, friend, and for years the biggest body of water I'd seen was one drip that leaked into my junk drawer.

cards.question: Jesus heads to the sea with His disciples, and nobody else tags along.
A large crowd follows Jesus from Galilee, Judea and Jerusalem. Where else are people coming from?

answers.text: Idumea and around Tyre and Sidon
Egypt and around Babylon and Nineveh
Rome and around Corinth and Athens

cards.question: People are traveling from all over to get to Jesus. What made them come?

answers.text: They heard what great things He was doing
They heard what new laws He was giving
They heard what signs the prophets foretold

cards.text: Friend, this is a whole stadium trying to squeeze through ONE exit at the same time. So Jesus gives His disciples a job.

cards.question: Down by the sea, Jesus asks His disciples to have a ___ ready for Him so the crowd won't crush Him.
Jesus has healed so many that everyone with a disease is pressing forward. What are they trying to do?

cards.text: And it's not just people. When the unclean spirits see Jesus, they fall down before Him, and they know EXACTLY who just walked in.

cards.question: The unclean spirits fall down before Jesus. What do they cry out?

answers.text: You are the Son of God

cards.question: Jesus wants the unclean spirits to keep shouting who He is so everyone hears.

cards.text: He warns them sternly not to make Him known. Then Jesus goes up on the mountain, and He's got some calls to make.

cards.question: Up on the mountain, who does Jesus call to come to Him?

cards.text: They come, and He appoints twelve of them as apostles to be with Him. Friend, I got called out of the back of a junk drawer, so I KNOW how big that moment is.

cards.question: Jesus will send the twelve apostles out to ___, and give them authority to drive out ___.

cards.text: Now the roster. First up is Simon, and Jesus hands him a brand new name.

cards.question: First on the list of the twelve, Jesus names Simon ___.
Jesus gives James son of Zebedee and his brother John a name too: Boanerges. What does it mean?

cards.text: Sons of THUNDER, friend, and here I am thrilled to death with Papa. Then come the rest: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus and Simon the Zealot.

cards.question: The last name on the list of the twelve is Judas Iscariot, and Mark says he is the one who betrayed Jesus.

findings.problem: The question asks where else people are coming from, but the correct answer omits the region beyond the Jordan from Mark 3:8. No later card covers it, so the walkthrough leaves the list of places incomplete.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on luck or prior Bible knowledge rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Card 3 asks for locations not yet revealed, card 10 for Jesus' unrevealed response, card 14 for mission details not yet explained, and cards 16, 17 and 19 for an arbitrary new name, an untranslated name and an unrevealed betrayal. Together with the unsupported 50/50 statement in card 2, these go beyond a few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: After the appointment itself is told in Mark 3:13-15, Mark 3:16-19 is a roster of names. Cards 15-19 spread that name list across five cards and turn its details into three choice cards. Peter's new name, Boanerges and Judas' betrayal could be included as standout details in the summary, but the list should not generate choice cards.

rule.text: The rule: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions Peter or provides any clue from which that name could be reasoned out. The blank therefore tests wording the baker has not seen rather than a meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
